data.title: Finding Marginal Probabilities from Two-Way Tables
data.description: Practice calculating the probability of a single category by summing across rows and columns when totals are hidden.

challenges.question: What is P(Under 1 mile)? Enter your answer as a decimal between 0 and 1 (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Add the counts in the "Under 1 mile" row (gives 40). Divide by the grand total (sum of all cells = 100).

challenges.question: What is P(Rock)? Enter your answer as a decimal between 0 and 1 (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Add the counts in the "Rock" column (gives 36). Divide by the grand total (sum of all cells = 80).

challenges.question: What is P(Grade 7)? Enter your answer as a decimal between 0 and 1 (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Add the counts in the "Grade 7" row (gives 40). Divide by the grand total (sum of all cells = 90).

challenges.question: What is P(Brand B)? Enter your answer as a decimal between 0 and 1 (round to 2 decimals).
challenges.hint: Add the counts in the "Brand B" column (gives 63). Divide by the grand total (sum of all cells = 120).

data.educationalContext: Calculating marginal distributions is an essential skill in data analysis, allowing you to find the overall probability of a single event from multivariate data without relying on pre-calculated totals.
